title: An agent's definition
description: The body of PUT /v1/agents/{key}, and of GET /v1/agents/{key}/definition, which answers an agent file's definition too. An agent file's frontmatter takes the same keys, with its body as instructions, and name, org, user and notify besides.

description.description: What the agent is for, in words a person reads.

tools.description: What the agent may call: a tool the server ships, by name; files for the file tools over the agent's own tree and the trees it shares; server/* for every tool of an MCP server; workers/* for every tool the connected tool workers offer it; or * for all of them.

oneOf.description: A tree: org, org/name or org/@user/name.

shared.description: The trees shared with the agent, by the name each is seen under at shared/<name>/: a tree, or a tree and a mode, write unless it says read.

workspace.description: The trees the agent shares with other agents. Only trees the token's scope covers, and tools names files to reach them.

context.description: The files read into each turn, at most 20, in the agent's tree or one it shares, up to 16 KB of them unless max_bytes says. tools names files to read them with.

oneOf.description: A policy the server holds, by name.
Rules, as a policy file writes them.

timeout.description: How many seconds a turn may take.

idle_timeout.description: How many seconds the agent may have nothing to do before it sleeps, until something asks it. The server's default when absent.

max_iterations.description: How many rounds of tool calls a turn may make.

retries.description: How many seconds a turn waits before asking a model call again that failed for a passing reason, such as a timeout, one for each try: [1, 5] where neither this nor the host's defaults say. [] never asks again.

compaction.description: When the agent summarises its older history, as shares of the model's window; false never does.

name.description: The trigger's name, trigger-1, trigger-2 and so on by its place in the list where it is left out.

every.description: A cron expression, or a duration such as 30m.

prompt.description: What the agent is asked each time.

prompt_file.description: In place of prompt, a file in the agent's tree: each time, the agent is asked to read it and do what it says. tools names files to read it with.

overlap.description: What a firing does while a run is still going: skip it, or queue its prompt.

missed.description: What a trigger does about the firings it missed while down.

jitter.description: Up to this many seconds of delay, chosen at random each time.

triggers.description: The triggers that ask the agent something when they come round, each with a prompt or a prompt_file. A definition put again replaces them all, and PUT and DELETE /v1/agents/{key}/triggers/{trigger} change one. Any other field is the source's that the trigger watches, which one of them names; without one, it asks on every run. A trigger on a clock has every; a webhook has webhook and secret in its place, and is sent requests at POST /v1/hooks/{key}/{trigger}.

channels.description: The chat channels, as config.yaml names them, it may be chosen to answer in.
